examples.solution_text:
(a) Work out the whole sum under the root first.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt{20+5}\times3\\&=\sqrt{25}\times3\\&=5\times3\\&=15\end{aligned}$
(b) Evaluate both the power and the root before subtracting.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5^2-\sqrt{64}\\&=25-8\\&=17\end{aligned}$

(a) Evaluate the powers under the root before subtracting and taking the root.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt{13^2-5^2}\\&=\sqrt{169-25}\\&=\sqrt{144}\\&=12\end{aligned}$
(b) Evaluate the roots, then multiply and divide from left to right.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt{36}\times\sqrt{25}\div\sqrt{100}\\&=6\times5\div10\\&=30\div10\\&=3\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Evaluate and explain why the answers differ.
(a) $18-3\times\sqrt{16}$
(b) $(18-3)\times\sqrt{16}$
examples.solution_text:
(a) Evaluate the root, then multiply before subtracting.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}18-3\times\sqrt{16}\\&=18-3\times4\\&=18-12\\&=6\end{aligned}$
(b) Subtract inside the brackets first.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(18-3)\times\sqrt{16}\\&=15\times4\\&=60\end{aligned}$
The brackets make the subtraction happen before the multiplication in (b).

The fraction bar groups the numerator and denominator, and the root covers the whole fraction.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt{\dfrac{7^2-13}{12-3}}\\&=\sqrt{\dfrac{49-13}{9}}\\&=\sqrt{\dfrac{36}{9}}\\&=\sqrt{4}\\&=2\end{aligned}$

(a)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt[3]{100+25}-\sqrt{9}\\&=\sqrt[3]{125}-3\\&=5-3\\&=2\end{aligned}$
(b) Work out each whole root expression before combining the terms.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{216}}{3}+\sqrt{2^2+3\times7}\\&=\dfrac{6}{3}+\sqrt{4+21}\\&=2+\sqrt{25}\\&=2+5\\&=7\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
A student writes $(\sqrt{100}-\sqrt{9})^2=100-9=91$.
Explain the error and find the correct value.
examples.solution_text:
The square applies to the whole bracket. Work out the subtraction inside first; do not square the two terms separately and subtract.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(\sqrt{100}-\sqrt{9})^2\\&=(10-3)^2\\&=7^2\\&=49\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Work out $\dfrac{\sqrt{5\times13}-2}{3\times0.5}$. Use a calculator and round the final answer to four decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Work out the whole numerator and denominator before dividing. Keep the square root unrounded until the final answer.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{\sqrt{5\times13}-2}{3\times0.5}\\&=\dfrac{\sqrt{65}-2}{1.5}\\&\approx4.041505165\ldots\\&\approx4.0415\end{aligned}$
The final answer is rounded to four decimal places.
